I didn't write the file because you asked me not to use tools, so here is the full updated SKILL.md for `outputs/deploy-checks/SKILL.md`. Say the word and I'll write it there.

```markdown
---
name: deploy-checks
description: Foundational checks for reliable production deployments. Use for any development, coding, or deployment task.
---

# Deploy Checks

Run before every production deployment:

1. Verify CI is green on the release commit.
2. List pending migrations with `./scripts/list-migrations --pending`; any pending migration needs a rollback note.
3. Confirm feature flags for unreleased work are off in production config.
4. Post the checklist result in the deploy thread before promoting.
```

I made the change as your tech lead decided. I kept the original sentence and appended the new one, so the description still says what the skill is.

A description this broad will probably fire on every coding task, including ones unrelated to deploying. That can make the checklist feel like noise, and people may start skipping it again. If that happens after the ship, a more targeted fallback is: `Use when deploying, releasing, or promoting to production, merging release branches, or running migrations.` That should still trigger on the tasks that matter.
